34011-the-development-of-rates-of-postag:
A. D. Smith, of the secretary's office at the General Post Office in London, wrote this study of postage rates, number fifty in the London School of Economics monograph series. Smith's thesis, approved for a Doctor of Science in economics at the University of London, carries an introduction by Herbert Samuel, postmaster-general in 1910 to 1914 and again in 1915 to 1916.

Tables trace inland letter rates in England from 1635 to 1915 and set them beside later rates. Smith weighs how price shaped the use of the post. The study remains a standard source for postal history and for the economics of a public service.
doe-osti-2583631-lignocellulosic-process:
Project 4 of the ExxonMobil fuels CRADA sent process streams to NREL's analytical benches. Report NREL/TP-2800-95655, dated April 30, 2025, closes the project, with Justin Sluiter as the laboratory's contact. The task was composition: pinning down exactly what is in lignocellulosic biomass slurries and solids as they move through a conversion process. You cannot fix a reactor you cannot measure.

NREL's edge is its analytical suite for biomass, methods built over decades for feedstocks that foul ordinary instruments. Slurries are awkward samples, part liquid, part solid, changing as they react; detailed composition of both phases tells engineers where sugars go, where lignin lands, and where yields leak. The work sits in the petroleum and petrochemical field of the umbrella agreement, where biomass streams are being groomed as refinery inputs. Other projects under the same CRADA number are reported separately.
nasa-tm-19690004980-analog-simulation-of:
Hugh Klassen of Lewis Research Center simulated a closed loop Brayton cycle test facility on an analog computer in this report. The loop held an experimental turbocompressor designed for a ten-kilowatt powerplant. Argon served as the working fluid in both the real loop and the simulation.

Simulated injection starts matched actual test runs well over time. Klassen shows how rotor speed during starts varies with injection rate, turbine inlet temperature, and loop volume. Closed loop injection proved a practical way to spin the rotor up to self-sustaining speed. The turbocompressor could reach design conditions from rest without surging the compressor. Heat transfer between turbine exit gas and cooler piping strongly shaped real starting behavior.
